sourceTopic.title: 092 — Mixed Review 2
sentenceGoals: What do you do in the kitchen?

grammarExplanation: German question words often trigger verb-second order.
French question words can start a sentence.
Spanish question words carry an accent.
Chinese question words stay in the same position as the answer.
Japanese question words take particles like が or を.

en.text: What do you do in the kitchen?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: What → do → you → do → in → the → kitchen?
grammarExplanation: English word order: question word + auxiliary + subject + main verb.

de.text: Was machst du in der Küche?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: Was → machst → du → in → der → Küche?
grammarExplanation: German verb-second order in questions.
Question word + verb + subject + rest.

fr.text: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la cuisine?

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: Qu'est-ce → que → tu → fais → dans → la → cuisine?
grammarExplanation: French questions: question word + verb + subject + complement.
Inversion may be used in formal French.
Spanish questions: question word + verb + subject.
Question words carry a written accent.

analysis.literalOrderExplanation: 你在 → 廚房 → 做什麼？
grammarExplanation: Chinese word order stays the same in questions.
Question words replace the information being asked about.
